key_bets: Beam-driven non-equilibrium plasma can sustain T_i >> T_e at ~150–250 keV to suppress bremsstrahlung losses below fusion power output
FRC confinement scaling extrapolates successfully from C-2W's ~1 keV / 0.4 m separatrix to Da Vinci's ~250 keV / 1–2 m major radius (~150× temperature, 2.5–5× size)
Q_plasma ≥ 25–35 is achievable for p-B11 in a beam-driven FRC despite never having been demonstrated above unity in any confinement device
FRC tilt and kink instabilities remain controllable at multi-megaampere plasma currents via tangential NBI stabilization
NBI systems can be scaled to reactor-relevant proton beam energies (~250 keV) with acceptable wall-plug-to-plasma efficiency (η_NBI ≈ 0.20–0.35)
Inverse Cyclotron Converter (patent-stage) can achieve >90% direct conversion efficiency of MeV alpha particles at commercial scale
Continuous/steady-state FRC operation is achievable from the current ~30–40 ms pulse record to seconds-to-CW timescales
eliminated_costs: No tritium breeding blanket (no Li-6 enrichment, FLiBe, beryllium supply chain, or tritium extraction systems)
No heavy neutron shielding — thin water/boron shield instead of multi-meter composite structures, reducing building volume and structural steel
No REBCO/HTS superconducting magnet supply chain — near-unity FRC beta allows resistive copper coils at ~1 kG external field
No remote handling robotics — aneutronic fuel enables hands-on maintenance (ITER-class remote handling costs >$500M eliminated)
No tritium infrastructure — no radiological containment for primary circuit, tritium-compatible valves/pipes, or tritium accounting
novel_costs: NBI system as dominant capital driver (~$260M at $10M/MW × 26 MW, >50% of CAS22) with no commercial supply chain for reactor-scale high-energy NBI
Continuous NBI recirculating power burden (~100 MW wall-plug for 26 MW plasma at η_NBI=0.26) that cannot amortize over pulses and stays near-full-power at reduced capacity factor
Inverse Cyclotron Converter direct energy conversion system (~$127M per module in Branch C) — a patent-stage subsystem with no analog in other concepts
High-energy proton/deuterium beam sources, gas neutralization cells, and beam dump components at commercial scale — specialized NBI supply chain with no industrial manufacturing base
Continuous electrical power consumption for resistive copper coils (vs. one-time cryogenic setup for superconducting alternatives)

risks.description: Bremsstrahlung power balance may prevent any positive energy gain for p-B11 — at fully thermalized conditions, f_rad could exceed 0.80–1.0, forcing Branch A (no viable LCOE) regardless of Q_plasma
Temperature extrapolation from ~1 keV (C-2W/Norman record) to ~150–250 keV (Da Vinci target) represents a ~150× gap with no validated confinement scaling law for beam-driven FRCs
Q_plasma > 1 has never been demonstrated for p-B11 in any confinement device — Copernicus intermediate validation machine is unbuilt with no published parameters
FRC tilt/kink instabilities at reactor-scale major radii (1–2 m) and multi-megaampere plasma currents are unvalidated physics unknowns that directly determine whether Da Vinci can operate at all

NBI wall-plug-to-plasma efficiency is η_NBI ≈ 0.20–0.35 per C-2W data (two-step chain: source 0.55–0.65 × coupling 0.35–0.50), substantially worse than prior ~0.55 assumption, raising Q_plasma breakeven to ~14 and commercial minimum to 25–35

ICC direct energy conversion (>90% claimed) has zero experimental demonstration at MeV-range fusion product energies — without ICC, steam-baseline Da Vinci (~$119/MWh) cannot capture the economic value of aneutronic fuel choice

Capacity factor and NBI recirculating power interact multiplicatively — at sub-unity CF, NBI remains at full power for FRC stability, raising effective recirculating fraction and tightening Q_plasma floor beyond rated-power estimates
Continuous/CW FRC operation is undemonstrated — current experimental record is ~30–40 ms (NBI pulse-limited), with no demonstration of seconds-scale sustainment at reactor-relevant conditions

Da Vinci commercial specifications (fusion power, Q value, NBI system specs, plasma geometry, capital cost) are entirely unpublished — six blocking data gaps make the LCOE model physics-viability bounding rather than cost-estimation
No commercial manufacturing pathway exists for reactor-scale high-energy NBI systems — industrial scale-up of ion sources, neutralization cells, and power supplies is uncharacterized
NBI system lifetime and replacement schedule in a fusion radiation environment is unknown, making O&M cost structure (expected dominant driver) unpredictable
